realtime_memories.content: OpenBroadcast (~/Documents/Projects/GitHub/openbroadcast): Next.js 16 App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + hls.js live-TV player over the iptv-org dataset. Statically prerenders ~7.6k channel pages from a committed data/channels.approved.json; never calls iptv-org at request time. Public repo github.com/myselfRaifMondal/openbroadcast connected to Vercel Hobby (prj_QvYbgDmBaZd4ktme2R5TENoFpE8u, openbroadcast.vercel.app): push to main auto-deploys production (~4 min for the full catalogue). Name was inferred from the repo URL, not chosen; it lives in app/layout.tsx metadata + header and README. Renaming the Vercel project would break the URL.

Two catalogue modes via POLICY_MODE, both still working. 'public' = curated allowlist in scripts/policy.ts (four grounds for inclusion, then hard exclusions) -> 623 channels / 91 countries after pruning. 'open' (npm run filter:open) = no licensing or category filtering -> 7,648 / 174 countries, 266 sports; INCLUDE_NSFW=1 also keeps adult channels. Open is what ships. The curated policy code is retained, not deleted.

PUBLISHING DECISION (2026-08-30, user's explicit choice after I laid out the options): the public, unauthenticated site serves the FULL open catalogue — 7,648 channels including sports and pay-TV. main tracks the open snapshot. Do not re-litigate. The earlier open-mode honesty UI (unverified-basis labels, OPEN MODE badge, /policy banner) was then removed at the user's request — they asked to strip 'source and rules and regulations and everything'. Curated build is still one command away (npm run filter:channels, 623 channels). If they ever want the site gated: Vercel Authentication under Project > Settings > Deployment Protection (free on Hobby); the MCP Vercel connector 404s on this project so it must be done in the dashboard. The /policy route is deleted and returns 404 live.

Maintenance scripts: npm run filter:channels (curated build), filter:open (full catalogue), audit:candidates [minChannels] (owners clearing every hard exclusion but matching no allow rule — the allowlist review queue), check:streams [-- --prune] (two-pass stream probe, writes data/stream-health.json, records a streamHealth summary on the dataset, prunes only genuinely dead and never geo-blocked). Also: npm run build:search-index (and prebuild, which runs it automatically before next build).

Social/advertising assets live in brand/: five HTML artboards sharing brand/_base.css (same tokens as app/globals.css), rendered by brand/render.sh to brand/out/*.png at exact platform sizes — ig-feed 1080x1350, ig-story 1080x1920, linkedin 1200x627, whatsapp-status 1080x1920, square 1080x1080. render.sh drives the Chromium that Playwright already caches (~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1234/...) at 2x then sips-resamples down; no playwright npm dep is installed. Serve with `python3 -m http.server 4199` in brand/ first. NOTE: the Playwright MCP downscales screenshots (1080 -> 982), so never use it to produce fixed-size deliverables. Rules held: no broadcaster logos in adverts (implies endorsement), and every figure must match the current catalogue or the copy is a false claim.

Stream health / dead-channel pruning (measured 2026-08-30, open catalogue). Two-pass probe: 10s timeout at 64-way, then every failure retried at 20s/40-way — the retry recovered 296 of 1,964 apparent failures (15%), so NEVER prune on a single pass. Final: 7,108 live, 540 geo-blocked, 1,668 dead pruned (9,316 -> 7,648 channels, 174 countries, 266 sports). Geo-blocked (403/451) are deliberately NOT pruned — healthy streams the broadcaster fences to its own country; they play in-country or over VPN, and the curated public/government set geo-blocks hardest (15.7% vs 4.4% commercial). Health is a snapshot: iptv-org endpoints rot continuously, so re-run and re-prune periodically. Open follow-up offered but not built: surface health in the UI (sort/grey dead) so the catalogue self-corrects between probes.

UI is a broadcast-test-card design, rebuilt 2026-08-30 in the shape of a streaming front page (user asked for 'Twitch kind of UI'). Palette = desaturated SMPTE colour bars used as GENRE CODING, not decoration — categoryColor() in lib/channels.ts maps each genre to a bar colour used on card stripes, chips, and idents. Type: Archivo (display, uppercase tracked) + IBM Plex Sans (body) + IBM Plex Mono (data). Signature motif = the seven bars (.bars / .testcard in globals.css): logo mark, tuning state, and the test card shown for a dead feed. Structure: left rail (Sidebar.tsx, most-carried channels, localStorage via useSyncExternalStore), genre shelves (ChannelRow.tsx), full grid (ChannelBrowser.tsx), hero that opens on live TV and scans past dead feeds (HeroTuner.tsx). Keys: R surfs random, / focuses search. Search: a global command palette (SearchPalette.tsx) opens from any page with / or Cmd/Ctrl-K — the user specifically asked for search while watching, so it must stay reachable mid-programme; it fetches public/search-index.json (~470 KB, written by the prebuild script, gitignored) on first open rather than shipping 7.6k channels as page props. ChannelBrowser's own input is 'Filter this grid' and binds no key: one key, one meaning. Footer credits 'Raif Mondal' (their preferred short form — LICENSE still carries the full legal name 'Raif Salauddin Mondal', left deliberately). Player (components/Player.tsx) uses CUSTOM live controls, never <video controls>: the native bar's seek bar + duration is the grammar of a recording and misrepresents a broadcast (it also produced a '0:00' timecode under dead feeds — the user spotted this). No progress bar or duration anywhere; instead a LIVE pill that becomes 'Go live · Ns behind' and seeks to the edge. CRITICAL: measure drift against hls.js liveSyncPosition, NOT seekable.end — healthy HLS sits 15-20s behind the manifest edge by design, so measuring from the edge labels live playback as behind (my first version did exactly that). Player also auto-walks past dead mirrors before showing No signal. Keys: space/k, m, f.

NEVER fabricate metrics in this UI. User asked for Twitch-style live viewer counts; there is no analytics source for broadcasters' HLS feeds, so I built the layout without them and said why. Substitutes used instead, both real: 'Most carried' ranks by number of mirrored feeds (reach()), and recommendations are similarity-only (genre -> country -> reach), never claimed as personalised. Real per-site viewer counts would need an API route + Vercel KV and would mostly read 1. Related: verify player changes against a real stream via Playwright (video.readyState/currentTime/videoWidth), not an HTTP 200 — a channel page returns 200 while the stream is dead or geo-blocked. Confirmed live: BBC News, Red Bull TV, TVR 1, ABC News AU. Geo-fenced: Rai 1, TyC Sports. eslint here forbids setState-in-effect; use render-phase adjustment or useSyncExternalStore.
Probe is running. SSRF address guards pass all 17 cases including cloud-metadata (`169.254.169.254`) and IPv4-mapped loopback, while correctly *allowing* `172.32.0.1` just outside the private range.
